question: Sharad Purnima is associated with the Goddess _______ in some parts of India.
solution:
The correct answer is__** Lakshmi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Sharad Purnima is a harvest festival celebrated in some parts of India, especially in the northern regions.
 
• This festival is also known as** Kojagiri Purnima and is celebrated on the full moon day of the Hindu lunar month of Ashvin.**
 
• On this day, people worship Goddess Lakshmi, who is believed to bless them with wealth, prosperity, and happiness.
 
• The festival is celebrated with much fervor and enthusiasm, with people lighting lamps, singing and dancing, and preparing special dishes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 

** Gauri**

 
• Gauri is another name for Goddess Parvati, who is the consort of Lord Shiva.
 
• She is worshipped as the goddess of fertility, love, and devotion.
 
• However, Sharad Purnima is not specifically associated with Gauri in any part of India.

**Parvati**

 
• Parvati is one of the most popular goddesses in Hindu mythology and is worshipped as the mother goddess.
 
• She is also known as Shakti, the divine feminine energy, and is associated with fertility, power, and strength.
 
• While Sharad Purnima is associated with the goddess Lakshmi, Parvati is also worshipped on this day in some parts of India.

** Sita**

 
• Sita is the wife of Lord Rama and is worshipped as the ideal wife and mother.
 
• She is also known for her devotion and sacrifice, and is considered a symbol of purity and virtue.
 
• However, Sharad Purnima is not specifically associated with Sita in any part of India.

** Lakshmi**

 
• Lakshmi is the Hindu goddess of wealth, prosperity, and abundance.
 
• She is worshipped on Sharad Purnima as it is believed that on this day, she visits the earth and blesses her devotees with wealth and happiness.
 
• The festival is also known as Kojagiri Purnima, which means the night when Goddess Lakshmi is worshipped.
